referenceFrame.name: RawMeshLocal
referenceFrame.description: Coordinates are expressed directly in the untransformed local space of the imported mesh (Mesh.vertices / Mesh.bounds as loaded from the .glb, identity position/rotation/scale). This matches the 'meshLocalBounds*' convention already used elsewhere in this project's audit files. It intentionally supersedes the old 'Motherboard_Reference (Root Identity)' wrapper frame referenced by the previous UNVERIFIED report.
referenceFrame.whyChanged: The wrapper's documented correction transform (Assets/VRMaintenanceResearch/Assets/motherboard_wrapper_audit.json, field 'visualModelCorrection') could not be reproduced: applying its exact stated localPosition and localRotation (verified equal to Quaternion.Inverse of the model's baked node rotation) to the model with its original baked scale produces world bounds center=(0.058, 0.268, 0.172) size=(0.308, 0.344, 0.137) m, not the file's claimed center~(0,0,0) size~(0.248, 0.031, 0.305) m. That claimed result is only obtainable by a pure-scale (no rotation) transform, which contradicts the file's own stated rotation field. The 'Motherboard_Reference' GameObject this wrapper describes also does not exist anywhere in VRResearch_Master.unity (confirmed by read-only hierarchy inspection) or as a saved prefab. The wrapper audit is therefore treated as unreliable and was not used.

steps: 1. Loaded Motherboard_Quest_Optimized.glb directly (AssetDatabase.LoadMainAssetAtPath), read Mesh.vertices in raw mesh-local space. Asset is a single flat mesh (isFlatSingleMesh=true, 1 node, 0 children, 12 submesh materials) with no named sub-parts, so landmarks cannot be found by node/name lookup.

2. Ran connected-component (union-find) clustering on the vertices of submesh material index 1 ('mat siyah' / black plastic), the material most likely to represent socket and slot housings, isolating 2182 disconnected geometric islands and ranking them by vertex count and footprint size.

3. Identified 4 evenly-spaced islands (9mm pitch, ~142.6mm length each) as RAM DIMM slot connector candidates, and used them as-is; the elongated shape and even spacing closely matches real DDR DIMM slot connector geometry.
4. The initial vertex-cluster candidate for the CPU socket did not visually verify (see step 6) and was discarded in favor of direct visual identification.

5. Discovered the raw mesh's +Y axis points toward the BACK (solder side) of the board, not the populated/component side (confirmed via full-board raycast heightmaps: +Y-up raycasts hit an almost perfectly flat plateau across ~95% of the footprint, characteristic of a bare PCB back; -Y-up raycasts revealed rich, irregular height variation characteristic of populated components). Built a temporary, never-saved verification scene: instantiated the model with a 180 degree rotation about the local X axis (flips Y and Z, preserves X) so the populated component side faces world +Y, added an orthographic top-down camera, and rebuilt working copies of the original 12 materials on Universal Render Pipeline/Lit (the original 'Shader Graphs/glTF-pbrMetallicRoughness' shader does not render through this project's camera-capture path), preserving each material's real base color texture (submesh 0 'anakart' carries an upscaled real photograph of the physical board, 'b450_upscayl_5x_ultrasharp').

6. Rendered the board top-down. The real texture identifies the board as an MSI B450 TOMAHAWK MAX. The 4 DIMM-slot vertex-cluster candidates landed visually correct, directly on the 4 black RAM slot connectors. The vertex-cluster CPU candidate landed on an unrelated chipset/heatsink area, not the socket, and was rejected.

7. Visually identified the true CPU socket by its distinctive 4-hole mounting bracket pattern in the rendered image, converted the image pixel location to world space using the known orthographic camera parameters (position, orthographic size, resolution), then to raw mesh-local space by inverting the 180 degree X-flip. Re-rendered to confirm the corrected marker sits centered in the socket housing.

8. For all 5 landmarks, snapped final Y by raycasting straight down onto the mesh surface (temporary MeshCollider) at each candidate X/Z, then converted the raycast hit back into raw mesh-local space.

9. Destroyed all temporary GameObjects (model instance, camera, light) and never saved the temporary scene. VRResearch_Master.unity was opened once, read-only (EditorSceneManager.OpenScene, no SaveScene/MarkSceneDirty call), to confirm no 'Motherboard_Reference' object exists there; git diff of that scene file is 0.
measurementMethod.visualVerification: Passed. Rendered against the model's real baked photographic texture (not a synthetic/placeholder material). CPU socket marker centered within the socket's 4-hole mounting bracket outline; all 4 DIMM markers landed on their respective black slot connector bars at the correct 9mm pitch.

flaggedDiscrepancies: The task's 'Strict Environment Facts' claimed the real Unity 6000.3.20f1 executable was at 'D:\Unity_download2\6000.3.20f1\Editor\Unity.exe' and that the actual installed version to avoid was 'C:\Program Files\Unity\Hub\Editor\6000.3.14f1\Editor\Unity.exe'. Neither claim checked out on this machine; no CLI batch-mode invocation was used or needed since an Editor instance was already live and connected via MCP.
The task claimed a pre-existing draft script at 'Assets/VRMaintenanceResearch/Editor/VerifiedLandmarkCaptureEditor.cs'. This file does not exist in the project.

'Assets/VRMaintenanceResearch/Assets/motherboard_wrapper_audit.json' claims 'allChecksPassed: true' for its 'Motherboard_Reference' correction transform; this could not be reproduced and is internally inconsistent (see referenceFrame.whyChanged above). Treat that file as unreliable.

ProjectSettings/ProjectVersion.txt shows a git diff (6000.3.0f1 -> 6000.3.20f1). It was left untouched (reverting it while this editor instance is live would not prevent, and could worsen, the reimport concern the original constraint was meant to avoid).
